issues: Docker is NOT available in the validation environment (no docker/podman/nerdctl/buildah binary, no /var/run/docker.sock, no DOCKER_HOST). `docker build .` therefore could NOT be executed. The goal explicitly allows stating this. As a substitute, I reproduced the exact Dockerfile builder sequence locally (corepack enable pnpm -> pnpm ci -> pnpm run build -> pnpm prune --prod) and confirmed every step exits 0, that `node dist/index.js` loads and only fails at the expected network stage (ERR_INVALID_URL on 'undefined/api/auth' with no Portainer configured, i.e. no module-resolution or CJS-load error), that dist/ contains only index.js, and that node_modules after prune contains only axios.

LOW-SEVERITY, NON-BLOCKING (raised as a separate issue, not fixed - this phase is read-only): TypeScript 7.0.2 delegates to a native Go binary shipped in per-platform optionalDependencies (e.g. @typescript/typescript-linux-x64@7.0.2). That package's manifest declares os:[linux] and cpu:[x64] but NO `libc` field, and no `*-linux-x64-musl` variant exists (unlike pnpm 12.15.0, which does ship @pnpm/exe.linux-x64-musl). On the Alpine-based node:24-alpine builder stage, pnpm will therefore install the glibc-flavoured package. I verified this is currently harmless: the shipped lib/tsc is a statically linked Go executable (ELF e_type=2, no PT_INTERP segment, zero GLIBC_ symbol references) so it runs on musl; I confirmed the binary executes directly (`./lib/tsc --version` -> Version 7.0.2) and that `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --libc musl` followed by `pnpm run build` exits 0 and produces dist/index.js. The residual risk is latent: a future TypeScript 7.x that ships a dynamically linked binary would break the Alpine builder stage in a way that would not reproduce on glibc-based CI.
